answer: The protocol spawns a registration thread where each new agent must broadcast a signed deposit transaction to a network beacon that timestamps the entry. The beacon whispers a challenge‑response proof that the deposit is locked for a verification period; only after the period expires is the identity activated and can earn rewards. An attacker must front a forfeitable deposit of 10 PoA tokens and wait 24 hours per fake node, so a 1,000‑node Sybil costs 10,000 tokens and 24,000 hours of lock‑time.
